Illness status of contact reports

Source: R/contact_illness.r
contact_illness.Rd

Classifies the day described by each contact report (contact.date, the day before the report) as ill, healthy or unknown, following a longitudinal model of each participant in each season. A symptom report is not needed on the contact day itself.

Usage

contact_illness(
  contacts,
  symptoms,
  min.reports = 3,
  healthy = c("follow-up", "report"),
  chronic = c("none", "duration"),
  chronic.days = NULL,
  follow_up_end = c("last_healthy", "end_of_illness")
)

Arguments

contacts

a data table of contact reports with columns global_id and contact.date, and season if the symptom reports have one

symptoms

a data table of symptom reports, as returned by extract_data, with columns global_id, date, no.symptoms, symptoms.start.date, symptoms.end.date and symptoms.end.option. The columns ili (symptom-based ILI), ili.fever (symptom-based ILI with fever), ili.self (self-assessed ILI) and resp.symptoms (ARI) are used where present; a missing column gives missing flags. The column same (the answer to whether the symptoms are the same as in the previous report) is used where present, and the symptom columns that aggregate_symptoms derives the definitions from, so that bouts can be reconstructed and classified as in bouts_of_illness.

min.reports

the minimum number of days with symptom reports for a participant to be eligible in a season

healthy

the rule for a day outside a bout within follow-up: "follow-up" counts it as healthy, "report" only if a later report without symptoms covers it

chronic

an optional heuristic for chronic symptom reports: "none" (the default) applies no rule; "duration" treats reports with a valid interval of more than chronic.days days as chronic. This is an assumption: a long duration alone does not show that symptoms are chronic, and no rule for identifying chronic-only reports has been agreed. A chronic condition is deliberately unused, because people with one can also have an acute illness.

chronic.days

the number of days beyond which a report counts as chronic, for chronic = "duration"

follow_up_end

where follow-up ends: "last_healthy" (the default) at the last report without symptoms, or "end_of_illness" at the later of that report and the last established illness day. A reported recovery is capped at the report date; a continuing illness without a recovery establishes illness only through the days supported by reports. Contact days after follow-up have unknown status. Reports excluded as chronic do not extend follow-up.

Value

the contact reports with added columns follow_up (see above), current_symptoms ("symptoms" or "no symptoms"), and a daily column current_* and a bout column bout_* for each of ili (symptom-based), ili_fever (symptom-based with fever), ili_self (self-assessed), all "ILI" or "no ILI", and ari ("ARI" or "no ARI"). Each is missing where the information is lacking

Details

Eligibility and follow-up. A participant is eligible in a season if they filed symptom reports on at least min.reports different days and at least one of them reported no symptoms. Follow-up runs from the first report without symptoms to the end given by follow_up_end. Bouts are reconstructed from all symptom reports, including those of ineligible participants and those outside follow-up; eligibility and follow-up only decide which contact days are classified. The column follow_up records the result: "in follow-up", "before follow-up", "after follow-up" or "not eligible". Contact days outside follow-up have an unknown status and are never called healthy.

Bouts. Bouts and the days of illness come from bout_evidence, the same reconstruction as in bouts_of_illness: the answer to whether the symptoms are the same as at the previous report, the dates of onset and recovery, and intervening reports without symptoms decide which reports form a bout. A report with a start and an end date (the end counted no later than the report) supports the days between them. A report of continuing illness supports the days from its start date to the report date, or only the report date when it gives no start date: the onset is then unknown and the days before it are unknown, but the report date is a day of illness, and a contact describing it is classified as ill. Recovery on that date, or illness on the following one, is not established. Days between known illness days of the same bout are included as continuing illness. The first symptomatic report is retained by the shared reconstruction even when onset is unknown. Missing onset may be recovered from other reports assigned to that same bout.

Case definitions of bouts. The symptoms of all reports of a bout are combined first and the definitions applied to the result, so symptoms reported in different questionnaires of one bout can jointly meet a definition (see bout_evidence). Where the data lack the symptom columns a definition is built from, it is positive if any report of the bout is. Two adjacent illnesses that the answers separate keep their own definitions.

Daily status. Within follow-up, current_symptoms is "symptoms" on days in a bout. With healthy = "follow-up" every other day is "no symptoms", with or without a report that day. With healthy = "report" a day is "no symptoms" only if a report without symptoms filed after it covers it, from the date of the previous report up to the day before its own. Days before a participant's first report, and days with no such report, are unknown. The exception is a report with symptoms (or without a known symptom status) whose dates give no usable interval: missing, inconsistent, or an unknown end that is not "still ill". Its illness cannot be placed, so every day since the participant's previous report, up to and including its own date, is unknown (missing) unless it lies in a bout. The same holds for the days before the report date of a continuing illness without a start date. A continuing-illness report also leaves the days after its date until the next report unknown unless bout evidence covers them. A report without symptoms is taken as no acute illness. By default (chronic = "none") the function applies no rule for chronic symptoms. With chronic = "duration", the function treats reports flagged by that assumption as no acute illness. Such reports support no bout and leave no day unknown.

The case-definition flags are known per report, not per day. A bout meeting a definition at some point need not have had every symptom present on every day of it. The bout_ columns therefore describe the whole bout and are the ones for bout-based exposure: positive on every day of a bout that meets the definition on the combined symptoms of its reports, negative if the combined evidence rules it out, and missing otherwise. Uncertain report dates do not change a bout flag on only some days. The daily current_ columns are positive or negative within a bout only on dates with a symptom report whose interval covers that date, assuming that such a report describes its own day, and are missing on other days of a bout: the symptoms of those days are not known, but the participant is known to be ill. Several reports on a day are combined: positive if any is positive, otherwise missing if any is unknown. Outside bouts, within follow-up and where status is not unknown, both are negative. The four definitions (symptom-based ILI, with fever, self-assessed ILI and ARI) stay separate.

Read the symptom data with a clean argument in extract_data that cannot drop symptom reports, as the default cleaning (e.g., "remove.first") can remove reports that support a bout. Use clean = c("unsuccessful.join", "remove.bad.symptom.dates") to clear invalid symptom dates without dropping reports when reading a single survey. Cleared dates leave the report without a usable interval, which is handled as above. If both tables have a season column, eligibility, follow-up and bouts are determined per participant and season.

Examples

contacts <- extract_data(
  simulated_data, years = 2013:2014, surveys = c("background", "contact")
)
symptoms <- extract_data(
  simulated_data, years = 2013:2014, surveys = "symptom",
  clean = c("unsuccessful.join", "remove.bad.symptom.dates")
)
table(contact_illness(contacts, symptoms)$current_symptoms, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#> no symptoms    symptoms        <NA> 
#>        1012          71         742
